item.title: Ilia Malinin fights for NHK Trophy title, extends Grand Prix figure skating win streak
item.description: Ilia Malinin followed his record short program by fighting through a strong free skate to win NHK Trophy, his ninth consecutive Grand Prix figure skating title dating to 2023. Malinin, the three-time world champion, doubled his planned quadruple flip to open his free skate to music from the animated series Blue Eye Samurai. He landed four quads later in his program, two of them a quarter under-rotated. It was still plenty enough as Malinin totaled 305.31 points and won by 34.82 over Frenchman Kevin Aymoz in Tokyo. "It felt like a battle out there, and I think it kind of represented the character that I play in this song," Malinin told the crowd. "I was not feeling the best today, but I tried my hardest to push through the whole program." FIGURE SKATING: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule Malinin beat his score from Saatva Skate America (284.31) and became the first man to break 300 points this Grand Prix season, which is now six events deep. Only the Grand Prix Final two weeks from now in China remains, which Malinin won the last three years. The Final takes the top six skaters per discipline over the six regular season events. It's the second-most prestigious annual competition after March's World Championships and the most exclusive. Earlier Saturday, Americans went one-two in ice dance with world bronze medalists Emilea Zingas and Vadym Kolesnik and Christina Carreira and Anthony Ponomarenko. Zingas and Kolesnik won with 203.29 points, the world's third-best total score over six Grand Prix regular season events. Only Olympic gold medalists Laurence Fournier Beaudry and Guillaume Cizeron of France's two scores this season have been higher. Zingas and Kolesnik and Fournier Beaudry and Cizeron will go head-to-head for the first time this season at the Grand Prix Final. Carreira and Ponomarenko, who were second or third at the last four U.S. Championships, finished second and third at their two Grand Prix starts this season to qualify for the Final for the first time in the sixth and last spot. Shin Ji-A of South Korea overtook Mone Chiba to win the women's NHK title and deny Japan a sweep of the six Grand Prix regular season women's titles. Shin, 18, made her first senior Grand Prix podium in her second season on the circuit. She's the first South Korean skater to win a Grand Prix since Kim Ye-Lim in 2022. But Shin did not qualify for the Final as her other Grand Prix result this fall — sixth at Skate Canada — wasn't strong enough. Chiba, who won Cup of China, fell on a downgraded triple loop in her NHK free skate, but still qualified for the Final in the third spot behind countrywomen Ami Nakai and Mao Shimada. They'll be joined at the Final by Alexandra Ignatova from Russia, Niina Petrokina from Estonia and Anastasiia Gubanova from Georgia. American Isabeau Levito is the first alternate. World champions Minerva Hase and Nikita Volodin won the pairs' event, just as they did at Skate America, to qualify for the Final. Ilia Malinin starts next figu

item.title: Urban Meyer gives common sense recommendation to USC’s Lincoln Riley ahead of UCLA game
item.description: The USC Trojans close the regular season Saturday against the UCLA Bruins with an 8-3 record, and losses to the Oregon Ducks, Wisconsin Badgers and Indiana Hoosiers have kept Lincoln Riley’s fifth season in Los Angeles under steady scrutiny. Urban Meyer, the former Ohio State coach who now works as a Fox Sports analyst, laid out what he would do about Riley on this week’s episode of The Triple Option, the podcast he hosts with Rob Stone and Mark Ingram II. Jan 20, 2025; Atlanta, GA, USA; Urban Meyer looks on during the second half the CFP National Championship college football game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images “USC is probably right behind Oregon as far as talent. Now, they don’t always play that way. “I don’t think they should move on from Riley. Keep Lincoln Riley, hire an offensive coordinator. Lincoln Riley has to go sit in defensive meetings. He’s got to go sit in special teams meetings. He’s got to quit the stupid penalties. He’s got to do the head coach things,” Meyer said. URBAN MEYER WEIGHS IN: Former national championship-winning head coach and FOX Sports analyst Urban Meyer weighed in on the future of #USC HC Lincoln Riley during an appearance on The Triple Option Show. Meyer believes USC possesses one of the most talented rosters in the Big Ten but acknowledged that the Trojans don’t consistently perform up to their potential. “USC is probably right behind Oregon as far as talent. Now, they don’t always play that way.” Despite USC’s inconsistencies, Meyer doesn’t believe the Trojans should move on from Riley. Instead, he believes Riley needs to hire an offensive coordinator and become more involved in overseeing every aspect of the program. “I don’t think they should move on from Riley. Keep Lincoln Riley, hire an offensive coordinator. Lincoln Riley has to go sit in defensive meetings. He’s got to go sit in special teams meetings. He’s got to quit the stupid penalties. He’s got to do the head coach things.” Meyer’s comments raise an interesting question surrounding the structure of USC’s coaching staff and whether Riley’s responsibilities as an offensive play-caller are limiting his effectiveness as a head coach. Five seasons into the Lincoln Riley era, is it time for Riley to relinquish offensive play-calling duties? : Icon Sportswire — Trojans Zone (@TrojansZone) November 27, 2026 Luke Huard is in his second season as USC’s offensive coordinator , with Riley calling the plays, so the hire Meyer described would mean handing the play sheet to someone else. Riley hired Gary Patterson, who led TCU for 21 seasons and was named to the College Football Hall of Fame class of 2026, to run the defense this season. “I’m certainly feeling his impact of just having a fellow head coach in the building, somebody else that has sat in this chair and make some of these decisions,” Riley said at Big Ten media days in July. Rebilas-Imagn Images “USC is probably right behind Oregon as far as talent. Now, they don’t always play that way. “I don’t think they should move on from Riley. He’s got to do the head coach things,” Meyer said. Meyer believes USC possesses one of the most talented rosters in the Big Ten but acknowledged that the Trojans don’t consistently perform up to their potential. “USC is probably right behind Oregon as far as talent. Now, they don’t always play that way.” Despite USC’s inconsistencies, Meyer doesn’t believe the Trojans should move on from Riley. Instead, he believes Riley needs to hire an offensive coordinator and become more involved in overseeing every aspect of the program. “I don’t think they should move on from Riley. Keep Lincoln Riley, hire an offensive coordinator. Lincoln Riley has to go sit in defensive meetings. He’s got to go sit in special teams meetings. He’s got to quit the stupid penalties. He’s got to do the head coach things.” Meyer’s comments raise an interesting question surrounding the structure of USC’s coaching staff and whether Riley’s responsibilities as an offensive play-caller are limiting his effectiveness as a head coach. Five seasons into the Lincoln Riley era, is it time for Riley to relinquish offensive play-calling duties? : Icon Sportswire — Trojans Zone (@TrojansZone) November 27, 2026 Luke Huard is in his second season as USC’s offensive coordinator , with Riley calling the plays, so the hire Meyer described would mean handing the play sheet to someone else. Riley hired Gary Patterson, who led TCU for 21 seasons and was named to the College Football Hall of Fame class of 2026, to run the defense this season. “I’m certainly feeling his impact of just having a fellow head coach in the building, somebody else that has sat in this chair and make some of these decisions,” Riley said at Big Ten media days in July. With a former head coach already running the defense, the change Meyer is asking for comes back to the hours Riley spends building and calling the offense. Riley has said he would give up play-calling if it helped Riley told ESPN’s Paolo Uggetti at those same media days that he weighed handing off play-calling during his second year at USC and decided to keep it. “I enjoy winning a whole hell of a lot more than calling plays. If I thought it would help us out I would do it in a heartbeat,” Riley said . Nov 29, 2025; Los Angeles, California, USA; Southern California Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava (14) and head coach Lincoln Riley react after the game against the UCLA Bruins at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images USC’s two lowest scoring totals this season came in road losses, seven points at Wisconsin on Oct. 24 and 13 at Indiana on Nov. 14. The same offense scored 30 in a home win over the Ohio State Buckeyes a week after the Wisconsin loss. The other loss, 41-27 to Oregon on Sept. 26, fell more on a defense that allowed 41. USC has been flagged 70 times for 606 yards through 11 games, while its opponents have been called for 62 penalties and 498 yards. The totals lump procedural flags together with the kind Meyer called stupid, but they show USC handing back 108 more penalty yards than it has gained from opponents’ mistakes. Meyer’s argument for keeping Riley starts with the roster, which he ranks just behind Oregon’s. His remedy asks Riley to give up the one job he has kept for himself through five seasons in Los Angeles, the same job he said in July he would surrender if it helped USC win. Riley went 11-3 in his first season at USC and 24-15 over the next three. A win over UCLA would give him 44 victories in Los Angeles, and of course, the headset question will be waiting for him once USC’s season is over. item.title: Serie A Preview: Como vs Juventus – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
item.description: Serie A Preview: Como vs Juventus – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia is the venue as Como and Juventus go head-to-head in a standout Serie A fixture on Sunday evening. Both sides head into proceedings amid a rich vein of form, looking to consolidate their respective positions in the league standings. Cesc Fabregas’ side have enjoyed an outstanding start to the campaign, collecting 26 points from their opening 12 matches and establishing a five-point cushion over the Bianconeri. Juventus arrive in Lombardy in improved form after recording consecutive victories across all competitions. However, Luciano Spalletti’s men face a stern examination against a side that have proved particularly difficult to beat on home soil. Match Preview Como Como continued their impressive European campaign with a 1-0 victory over AEK Athens on Tuesday. Luis Milla scored the decisive goal at the start of the second half, securing a fourth win in five Champions League outings and keeping the Lariani firmly on course for the knockout stages. Fabregas’ side have also maintained their momentum in Serie A, where they sit fifth, only a point adrift of fourth-placed Milan. They bounced back from their defeat to Inter by beating Cagliari 2-0 last weekend, with Jacobo Ramón and Lucas Da Cunha finding the net. The hosts have won eight of their opening 12 league fixtures (D2, L2) and boast one of the division’s strongest defensive records. They have conceded just 10 goals, while their home form has been particularly impressive, with four victories and one draw from five matches. Como have also kept four consecutive clean sheets at the Sinigaglia, against Roma, Sassuolo, Venezia, and Cagliari. Another positive result would open up an eight-point gap over Juventus and strengthen their position in a fiercely contested top-four race. The Lariani also have fond recent memories of this fixture, having beaten Juventus 2-0 in both league meetings last season. They had not defeated the Turin giants at home in Serie A since 1952 before ending that long wait in October 2025. Juventus Juventus have gradually rediscovered their attacking confidence under Spalletti, winning their last two games across all competitions. After thrashing Venezia 4-0 in Serie A, the Bianconeri came from behind to defeat Omonia Nicosia 4-1 in the Europa League on Thursday. The Turin giants have now scored 14 goals in their last five outings, suggesting their attacking problems may finally be easing. However, their domestic campaign remains inconsistent, with six wins, three draws and three defeats leaving them sixth in the standings on 21 points. Juventus have also stuttered away from home, which spells trouble ahead of this showdown. Another positive result would open up an eight-point gap over Juventus and strengthen their position in a fiercely contested top-four race. The Lariani also have fond recent memories of this fixture, having beaten Juventus 2-0 in both league meetings last season. They had not defeated the Turin giants at home in Serie A since 1952 before ending that long wait in October 2025. Juventus Juventus have gradually rediscovered their attacking confidence under Spalletti, winning their last two games across all competitions. After thrashing Venezia 4-0 in Serie A, the Bianconeri came from behind to defeat Omonia Nicosia 4-1 in the Europa League on Thursday. The Turin giants have now scored 14 goals in their last five outings, suggesting their attacking problems may finally be easing. However, their domestic campaign remains inconsistent, with six wins, three draws and three defeats leaving them sixth in the standings on 21 points. Juventus have also stuttered away from home, which spells trouble ahead of this showdown. They have secured only two victories from six Serie A trips this season (D2, L2), scoring eight goals and conceding the same number. Their defensive record nevertheless offers encouragement. Juventus have kept six clean sheets in 12 league games, while only Como have registered more shutouts since Spalletti took charge last November. The Bianconeri have historically dominated this fixture, winning 15 of their 30 Serie A meetings with Como. However, last season’s setbacks underline how much the balance of power has shifted, meaning they would be naive to rest on their laurels here. Team News Como remain without Moise Kean, Willy Kambwala, and Jesus Rodriguez. Maxence Caqueret also faces a race against time to recover, while Assane Diao and Jayden Addai must pass late fitness tests. Tasos Douvikas should continue to lead the attack in Kean’s absence. The Greek striker has scored 11 goals across all competitions this season and will likely receive support from Da Cunha, Nico Paz, and Martin Baturina. Juventus have several important absentees of their own. Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, and captain Manuel Locatelli remain sidelined, while Nicolás Gonzalez and Pierre Kalulu face late fitness assessments. Nick Woltemade should retain his place up front after contributing to three goals across his last two Serie A appearances. Randal Kolo Muani and Francisco Conceicao are also expected to feature, with Douglas Luiz and Teun Koopmeiners likely to form the midfield partnership. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ATHENS, Ga. — Georgia football is preparing to make history against Georgia Tech on Saturday, but one former Bulldogs standout will find himself in an unusual position. His son is playing for the other team. Former Georgia running back Verron Haynes, who once delivered a memorable performance against the Yellow Jackets, will be supporting Georgia Tech as his son, Justice Haynes, attempts to upset the nation’s No. 1 team. The family connection adds another fascinating storyline to a rivalry already filled with bad blood. And this time, Georgia’s history is directly involved. Former Georgia Standout Faces Unusual Rivalry Decision Verron Haynes played for Georgia from 1999 through 2001, establishing himself as a productive running back before beginning his professional career. His most memorable performance against Georgia Tech came in 2001. Haynes rushed for 207 yards on 39 carries, helping the Bulldogs secure a victory over their in-state rivals. More than two decades later, his son is preparing to face Georgia from the opposite sideline. Justice Haynes, who previously played at Alabama and Michigan, now represents Georgia Tech. The running back also has strong family connections to Athens. Both of his parents attended Georgia, making Saturday’s matchup particularly personal. Justice Haynes Reveals Where His Father’s Loyalty Stands Despite his family’s Georgia background, Justice Haynes made it clear that his father will support him Saturday. Speaking to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, Haynes explained that his parents have supported his football journey regardless of the program he represents. He also revealed that his father plans to wear Georgia Tech colors for the rivalry game. The admission provides an unusual twist to one of the South’s oldest college football rivalries. A former Georgia star who once helped defeat Georgia Tech will now be cheering for the Yellow Jackets. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ATHENS, Ga. — Georgia football is preparing to make history against Georgia Tech on Saturday, but one former Bulldogs standout will find himself in an unusual position. His son is playing for the other team. Former Georgia running back Verron Haynes, who once delivered a memorable performance against the Yellow Jackets, will be supporting Georgia Tech as his son, Justice Haynes, attempts to upset the nation’s No. 1 team. The family connection adds another fascinating storyline to a rivalry already filled with bad blood. And this time, Georgia’s history is directly involved. Former Georgia Standout Faces Unusual Rivalry Decision Verron Haynes played for Georgia from 1999 through 2001, establishing himself as a productive running back before beginning his professional career. His most memorable performance against Georgia Tech came in 2001. Haynes rushed for 207 yards on 39 carries, helping the Bulldogs secure a victory over their in-state rivals. More than two decades later, his son is preparing to face Georgia from the opposite sideline. Justice Haynes, who previously played at Alabama and Michigan, now represents Georgia Tech. The running back also has strong family connections to Athens. Both of his parents attended Georgia, making Saturday’s matchup particularly personal. Justice Haynes Reveals Where His Father’s Loyalty Stands Despite his family’s Georgia background, Justice Haynes made it clear that his father will support him Saturday. Speaking to the Atlanta Journal-Constitution, Haynes explained that his parents have supported his football journey regardless of the program he represents. He also revealed that his father plans to wear Georgia Tech colors for the rivalry game. The admission provides an unusual twist to one of the South’s oldest college football rivalries. A former Georgia star who once helped defeat Georgia Tech will now be cheering for the Yellow Jackets. However, the decision reflects family loyalty rather than any publicly stated disagreement with Georgia. Justice has consistently emphasized the support he receives from his parents. Georgia Tech Has Opportunity to Ruin Bulldogs’ Historic Moment Saturday’s matchup carries additional significance for Georgia. The Bulldogs have defeated Georgia Tech in eight consecutive meetings, matching the longest winning streak in series history. Georgia Tech previously won eight straight games from 1949 through 1956. Now, Kirby Smart’s program has an opportunity to establish a new record with a ninth consecutive victory. However, the Yellow Jackets would love nothing more than to prevent that milestone. Georgia enters the matchup ranked No. 1 nationally with a 10-1 record. Meanwhile, Georgia Tech is 3-8 following a difficult season. The Bulldogs are favored by more than five touchdowns, according to betting lines reported by the Atlanta Journal-Constitution. Nevertheless, rivalry games can carry an emotional significance that extends beyond records and rankings. Georgia Once Recruited Justice Haynes The family connection becomes even more interesting when considering Justice Haynes’ recruiting history. Georgia recruited the running back during his high school career. However, Haynes ultimately chose Alabama before later transferring to Michigan and Georgia Tech. His journey has now brought him back to his home state, where he will face the program his father once represented. The matchup offers an opportunity to compete against one of the nation’s strongest defenses. Georgia enters Saturday allowing just 89.7 rushing yards per game. Meanwhile, Georgia Tech has relied on its running game to help offset uncertainty at quarterback. A productive performance from Haynes could help the Yellow Jackets challenge a heavily favored opponent. Kirby Smart Looks to Extend Georgia’s Dominance Georgia has controlled the rivalry throughout Smart’s tenure. The Bulldogs have won every meeting against Georgia Tech since 2017. Last season, Georgia secured a 16-9 victory in Atlanta. Now, the Bulldogs return to Sanford Stadium seeking another victory before their SEC Championship Game appearance against Texas. However, Georgia Tech has an opportunity to disrupt the Bulldogs’ momentum. The Yellow Jackets have struggled defensively throughout the season, allowing 31.5 points per game. Georgia, meanwhile, averages 41.1 points per contest. Those numbers suggest a difficult matchup for Georgia Tech. Still, the emotional stakes are considerable for both programs. A Georgia Family Will Be Wearing Different Colors For most Georgia fans, Saturday represents another opportunity to extend the Bulldogs’ dominance over their in-state rival. For the Haynes family, the afternoon carries a different meaning. Verron Haynes once helped Georgia defeat Georgia Tech with one of the most memorable rushing performances of his college career. Now, his son will attempt to help the Yellow Jackets accomplish the opposite. The former Bulldogs standout has made his priorities clear through his son’s account of the family’s support. On Saturday, he will be cheering for Justice. Even if that means wearing the colors of Georgia’s biggest in-state rival. item.title: Jørgen Strand Larsen: ‘Dad and I have been best mates since I was a kid – that’s not going to change’
item.description: Striker determined to raise prostate cancer awareness after father, who scored goals for fun at amateur level in Norway, received terminal diagnosis It is a fresh Friday afternoon at Selhurst Park and, after posing for a couple of pictures in front of the red and blue Holmesdale End, Jørgen Strand Larsen holds a scarf overhead in true new-signing style. This is not the last step before a routine announcement, nor is this a run-of-the-mill club, his manicured moustache a giveaway. The Crystal Palace and Norway striker has joined forces with Prostate Cancer UK to raise awareness of the disease after his father, Atle Wester, was given a terminal diagnosis this year. Strand Larsen arrives after a recovery session following Thomas Frank’s first victory since taking charge. He devotes more than an hour to learning more about a subject close to his heart, meeting Dr Matthew Hobbs, the charity’s research director, before a round-table conversation with Mark Bright, a Palace ambassador, and a couple of fans with links to the cause. Continue reading...

item.title: Basque to the future: Andoni Iraola fired up for first Merseyside derby
item.description: Liverpool head coach sees parallels with Athletic v Sociedad derby as he comes up against his old foe David Moyes “I haven’t lived this derby,” Andoni Iraola acknowledged, and yet he already feels it. A former Athletic Bilbao captain coming up against an ex-Real Sociedad head coach needs no instruction on the importance of winning a derby, whether in the Basque country or on Merseyside. But this week, as the Liverpool head coach approaches his first experience of the latter, there has been no escape. “It has been very easy for me here,” says Iraola of his five months on Merseyside. “Family-wise we have settled in really well. People here are very friendly, they love to talk to you but in a very respectful way. This week there has been a lot [of interaction with Liverpool fans], especially with playing big games against United and Everton. ‘We need to win, we need to win,’ they say.” Continue reading...

item.title: USWNT seal Women’s World Cup qualification with 8-0 win over El Salvador
item.description: US goes up 7-0 over El Salvador by half-time Win secures spot at 2027 World Cup and 2028 Olympics The United States’ place at a Women’s World Cup is treated as a foregone conclusion, but Friday’s all-or-nothing qualifier against El Salvador gave some reason for nerves. This was the first competitive game for Emma Hayes’ team since their Olympic gold medal match in August 2024, the end of two years of only friendlies. Given the global advances in women’s soccer over the years, maybe El Salvador could spring an all-time upset. The suspense ultimately lasted for eight minutes and 20 seconds. The USWNT opened the scoring in their Concacaf W Championship quarter-final with El Salvador in the ninth minute; a nifty training-ground set piece routine ending with Kennedy Wesley prodding the ball into the net, putting the hosts in the driver’s seat for an 8-0 win and a spot in next summer’s big show. With the win, the US maintains their perfect Women’s World Cup attendance record, a part of all 10 tournaments to date. Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta sets Arsenal 100-point Premier League target to emulate Manchester City

City head to the Emirates Stadium on Sunday already trailing Arsenal by six points after just 11 games, with Enzo Maresca’s side having failed to win any of their four previous league matches. item.title: Spygate tensions erupt at Southampton after Finn Azaz’s cry-baby celebration riles Boro
item.description: When asked whether he had any regrets about running the length of the pitch to goad the Middlesbrough supporters he used to call his own with a mock crying celebration, Finn Azaz was unequivocal. “None whatsoever,” said the Southampton playmaker. And you get the sense that very few associated with his club disagreed. Southampton, and their manager Tonda Eckert, long ago admitted their Spygate crime. Based on the behaviour of many connected to the south-coast club – their manager a notable exception – they have embraced it. item.title: Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus fire Nottingham Forest past shaky Chelsea
item.description: Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he invited opprobrium by making light of missing a penalty at Liverpool in an unsanctioned French interview, he endured the ultimate ignominy when Chelsea supporters followed a four-letter suggestion to tell the defender: “You’re not welcome here.” Fofana was humiliated by Liam Delap before fouling the former Chelsea striker for a penalty that Morgan Gibbs-White converted for the first of his two goals. The result, coming after Forest’s win against Manchester City in their last match at the City Ground, means they climb three points clear of the Premier League’s relegation zone. Continue reading...

item.title: Why have things started to go wrong for Manchester City under Enzo Maresca?
item.description: A sensational start for the Italian was swiftly followed by a dismal run and long faces in the team This is the great known unknown in Manchester City’s run of one win – in addition to victory on penalties against Brighton in the Carabao Cup – in seven matches. After guilty verdicts were returned regarding the breaking of Premier League financial rules, Enzo Maresca’s team went to Anfield and handed Liverpool a 3-0 schooling . Yet this proved the falsest of dawns, with Andoni Iraola’s nascent side perhaps caught in a bad moment. City have since managed one league victory ( 3-2 over Ipswich , six days later) and two more wins in regulation time (in the Champions League) in 10 matches. The sequence includes one point from the past four league fixtures. Maresca argues that his, too, is an embryonic project so there will be uneven form. “I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. City have appealed against the ruling, saying they are “innocent of the accusations”. Continue reading...

item.description: Club activate option and plan further talks with captain ‘I am not nice,’ says Pochettino as he targets improvement Manchester United have triggered a clause to extend the captain Bruno Fernandes’ contract until the summer of 2028 on a day when Mauricio Pochettino warned his players they should not expect him to be “nice” in his attempts to turn around the club’s fortunes. Fernandes’ deal was due to expire in June and by exercising the option United have avoided the risk from January that he could negotiate a pre-contract agreement with a club abroad to join on a free next summer. Fernandes said this month that talks over a longer extension were on hold “because of the context of the team and the club”. He has turned down two United contract offers. Continue reading...

item.title: Ross County have 102 goals and British football’s best start but is it a fairytale?
item.description: There is cynicism and jealousy but one of County’s top scorers is 39 as club try to climb leagues again after tumbling It was a vidiprinter moment worthy of a double take. Ross County 1 Cove Rangers 1 (Keir 52). Would Cove, scrapping for survival in Scottish League One, put an unlikely end last Saturday to the most emphatic run in British senior football? Don’t be silly, retorted County; four goals in the closing 17 minutes extended the Dingwall side’s goal difference to plus 45 (for 56, against 11). Played 16, won 14, drawn two. There is as much chance of Mike McCarthy settling down for Christmas dinner with Aaron Rodgers as there is of County missing out on promotion back to Scotland’s second tier. Taking in cup competitions they have scored 102 goals this season. An assessment from the captain, Brian Graham, of a frankly irrelevant loss on penalties to Stenhousemuir in the Challenge Cup epitomises the County approach. “We should have been five- or six-nil up at half-time,” an irked Graham says. “That shows the standards we have set. We lost a dubious goal, which shouldn’t have stood.” Earlier in that competition County whacked 14 past a Hearts youth side before defeating a Celtic B team including two Chelsea loanees and a £3m midfielder. Continue reading...

item.title: Can Borussia Dortmund finally end their title wait? Three big questions for Bundesliga leaders
item.description: Niko Kovac’s team lead the way and, with Bayern Munich wounded, have a golden chance to be German champions for the first time in 15 years Borussia Dortmund’s dreams have a habit of becoming nightmares, like when they somehow handed Bayern Munich the Bundesliga title on the final day of the 2022-23 season. Or when an 89th-minute Arjen Robben goal won the 2013 Champions League final for the same opponents. Whenever Dortmund suffer heartbreak, it usually involves Bayern. As things stand, however, Niko Kovac’s side hold a two-point lead over Bayern at the top of the Bundesliga. Both teams are unbeaten, but Dortmund may be the more stable of the two at the moment, especially with Harry Kane expected to miss several months through injury. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. Simon Burnton Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
item.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

item.title: Éric Cantona: ‘If I regret something about the kung fu kick, it’s that I would love to kick him in another place’
item.description: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.” It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil . Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United , whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Bayern Munich go from bad to worse with own goals on and off the pitch
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian. I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner. The constant change in Watford manager, a once fine club whose first two managers lasted a total of 23 years, is now so high that I don’t even notice it anymore ... apparently this was yesterday, and I’ve no idea who the previous bloke was. Watford are now onto their 30th manager, including caretakers, although in practice they’re all just caretaker managers, since the Pozzos took over in 2012. I don’t know whether to laugh at, or cry for, the Watford fans (Narrator: it’s the former, obviously) – Noble Francis. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.dc:creator: Barry Glendenning
item.content:encoded: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian. I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner. item.title: Peter Storey obituary
item.description: Arsenal midfielder capped by England 19 times whose life after football suffered a drink-fuelled decline The footballer Peter Storey , who has died aged 81, was a tough-tackling midfielder for Arsenal when they won the double of the First Division championship and the FA Cup in 1971. Arsenal were only the fourth team to achieve the double at that point (it has since been won another nine times), and Storey, who appeared in 49 of the 51 league and FA Cup games that season, played as big a role as anyone in securing the honours with his defensive solidity, ball-winning skills, “good engine”, sound distribution and reliable occasional penalty taking. Continue reading...

item.title: Alejandro Garnacho and the curious case of Aston Villa’s outcast loanees | Ben Fisher
item.description: Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award. He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup . Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Manchester City get that empty feeling as they fail to win again
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Early in the second half of Tuesday night’s National League South match between Torquay United and Chesham, play was briefly suspended due to an ear-splitting din emitted over the Plainmoor public address system. “The game has stopped because the Torquay Tannoy system is making a loud noise that won’t stop,” posted Chesham on their Social Media Disgrace account. “I’m not kidding.” A sort of aural cross between an ocean liner’s foghorn and a party conference speech delivered by a senior member of the Reform party, it eventually stopped and play resumed with Torquay running out 2-1 winners. In this constantly changing world of global disruptions, uncertainties and risks, with social, political and economic disaffection seemingly on the rise everywhere, it’s genuinely heartening to know that some things never change . ‘Plus ça change, plus c’est la même chose’, as the late, great French writer Jean-Baptiste Alphonse Karr famously said, something that I’m sure Big Dunc is well aware of” – Noble Francis. May I be the 1,092nd correspondent to demand a review of the Letter o’ the Day award for Monday – and it be awarded to Declan Hackett for his letter foretelling the rescinding of the red card given to Lenny Yoro on Sunday? Given the precedent of awarding/revoking/re-awarding of the Afcon 2025 edition this would be entirely justified” – Peter Martin. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

item.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
item.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, four months before the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to victory at the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentinos Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | The game’s gone: has fantasy football been ruined by AI gafferbots?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Sometimes, the beautiful game can make Football Daily feel old. Even Monday’s ostensibly old-school fixture between Brentford and Everton felt like the future destroying the past. The analytics-coded hosts prevailed 4-0 and James Tarkowski was dismissed by the VAR overlords for a challenge that would have been considered “firm but fair” on the muddy pitches of our youth. “I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” a misty-eyed David Moyes sighed after the game, before heading to the team bus to rewatch the Battle of Santiago . If Sunday was Gary Neville’s Sistine Chapel [ Monday’s Football Daily ], then his commentary on the Fernando Torres goal for Chelsea against Barcelona must be his David ” – Ronnie McMahon. Regarding Declan Hackett’s assertion [ Monday’s letters ] that Donald Trump will be helping his mate Mauricio Pochettino by ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card, perhaps Poch should be careful what he wishes for: Trump may equally decide to get Michael Carrick reinstated, as he also has a bit of previous for that sort of thing” – Dexter O Riordan. In all the time that I have been watching football, I don’t think I have ever seen a player dismiss himself and be away down the tunnel before given a red card. Thanks James Tarkowski ” – Nigel Sanders. Brighton had only failed to win twice in the league since 5 September. A 1-1 draw with Leeds and a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool - their only opponents with double letters in their name. That bizarre hoodoo struck again at Hull on Sunday. Good good news for Seagulls fans is the only double-lettered encounters they have before hosting Hull in February are trips to Forest and Spurs. Even better news is that since that 1-1 draw with Leeds on 5 September, they have a 100% win record against sides without double letters and have not conceded a goal” – Dan Ashley (and no others). Continue reading...

item.title: Timothy Weah: ‘I don’t want to beg to be back in the national team’
item.description: Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad This was the USMNT’s summer. By extension, it was also that of the 26 players selected by Mauricio Pochettino to represent the nation at a home World Cup. It didn’t live up to expectations for all of them, and certainly not for Timothy Weah. “Obviously this summer wasn’t the best for me,” he says. Weah was one of eight players in the squad to have started all four of the US’s matches in Qatar in 2022. He remained a regular heading into this tournament but would ultimately start only one game in a campaign that came to an end at the hands of Belgium in the last 16 . “In every career you have moments where you’re a bit down, and you’re a bit in your head about things. I think the World Cup was definitely that for me,” Weah says. “On a personal level, I had to take a back seat and figure out where my place was in the squad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. Continue reading...

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
item.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

item.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017. 183 places Montenegro (16th/199th) 165 Kuwait (24/189) 160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173) 155 Cape Verde (27/182) 153 Central African Republic (49/202) 151 Libya (36/187) 146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195) 144 Moldova (37/181) 141 El Salvador (49/190) 136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Suzanne Wrack Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...

item.title: Sign up for the Moving the Goalposts newsletter: our free women’s football email
item.description: Get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week, featuring the insights of experts such as Ada Hegerberg and Magdalena Eriksson Join us as we delve deeper into the wonderful world of women’s football in our weekly newsletter. It is informative, entertaining, global, critical – when needed – and, above all, passionate. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more. Try our other sports emails: as well as the occasionally funny football email The Fiver from Monday to Friday, there are weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown , and our seven-day roundup of the best of our sports journalism in The Recap .
